books.title: Field Notes from a Catastrophe
books.subtitle: Man, Nature, and Climate Change
books.author: Elizabeth Kolbert
books.summary: Its central report—that human-caused warming was already measurable, disrupting physical and living systems, and demanding emissions cuts—has strengthened substantially. Particular local outcomes still combine climate forcing with land use, governance, and natural variability.

claims.claim: Human greenhouse-gas emissions are warming the atmosphere, ocean, and land rather than merely coinciding with a natural cycle.
claims.rationale: Multiple independent observations and attribution studies establish human influence as the dominant cause of recent global warming. Natural variability shapes individual years and regions but cannot reproduce the long-term global pattern.

claims.claim: Climate change is already altering glaciers, sea level, seasonal timing, species ranges, and weather extremes.
claims.rationale: Observed changes span the cryosphere, ocean, ecosystems, and extremes in every region. Attribution strength differs by phenomenon, but the cross-system conclusion is no longer prospective.

sources.title: IPCC AR6 ocean, cryosphere and sea level chapter

claims.claim: The book's local case studies can be read mainly as consequences of global warming.
claims.rationale: The selected cases illustrate mechanisms that broader attribution research supports. Exact local timing and damage also depend on development, habitat fragmentation, pollution, management, and internal variability, so climate is not a complete cause by itself.

sources.title: US Fifth National Climate Assessment overview

other_claims: Political delay increases cumulative climate risk.
Public understanding often lags observed ecological change.

books.title: The Uninhabitable Earth
books.subtitle: Life After Warming
books.author: David Wallace-Wells
books.summary: The book correctly presents warming as a cascade of compounding risks across health, food, fire, migration, and economies. Its dramatic upper-tail scenarios are physically possible rather than central forecasts, and 'uninhabitable' describes uneven harms, not one uniform planetary threshold.

claims.claim: Every additional increment of warming increases multiple, interacting risks rather than adding only a little more heat.
claims.rationale: IPCC assessments find escalating and increasingly compound hazards with each increment of warming. Magnitudes, interactions, adaptation, and regional vulnerability remain uncertain, so individual cascades should not be treated as fixed forecasts.

sources.title: IPCC AR6 synthesis summary for policymakers

claims.claim: Climate change is already increasing serious risks to human health, food systems, infrastructure, and displacement.
claims.rationale: Observed heat mortality and damages are clear, and risk rises across interconnected systems. Total future mortality and migration figures depend strongly on emissions, exposure, development, policy, and adaptation.

sources.title: FAO climate change, agriculture and food security

claims.claim: High-end warming scenarios expose genuine catastrophic risks, but they are not the same as the most likely outcome.
claims.rationale: Very high warming produces severe and sometimes irreversible risks, while current policy and technology trajectories are not identical to older worst-case emissions pathways. Risk management should retain plausible tails without presenting them as a single forecast.

other_claims: Climate damages are distributed highly unequally.
Political imagination affects which climate futures remain possible.

books.title: Losing Earth
books.subtitle: The Decade We Almost Stopped Climate Change
books.author: Nathaniel Rich
books.summary: The book accurately recovers a pivotal 1979–1989 period when climate science and diplomacy moved rapidly toward national attention. Calling it a lost near-solution overstates consensus and understates fossil-fuel interests, partisan change, international distribution, and the institutional work still required.

claims.claim: By the 1980s, human-caused warming was a serious scientific and governmental concern, not a recent discovery.
claims.rationale: World climate conferences, congressional attention, federal research, the 1988 creation of the IPCC, and early international negotiations document substantial awareness. Scientific uncertainty remained, but the basic greenhouse risk was plainly actionable.

claims.claim: The United States came meaningfully close to adopting national climate action before the issue hardened politically.
claims.rationale: Bipartisan hearings, executive-branch proposals, scientific coordination, and international meetings created a real opening. Whether it was 'close' depends on the counterfactual: no durable domestic coalition, enforceable international allocation, or implementation architecture had been secured.

sources.title: 1988 Congressional Record on the greenhouse effect

claims.claim: A small set of missed meetings and personal failures mainly explains why effective climate policy did not emerge in the 1980s.
claims.rationale: Contingent leadership mattered, but the account compresses fossil-fuel political economy, regional winners and losers, collective-action problems, institutional vetoes, policy design, and later organized obstruction. Those forces make the failure larger than a narrow tragedy of personalities.

other_claims: Climate politics became more polarized after 1989.
The prehistory of the UNFCCC shows both genuine momentum and unresolved distributional conflict.

books.title: The New Climate War
books.subtitle: The Fight to Take Back Our Planet
books.author: Michael E. Mann
books.summary: The book is well supported that organized climate messaging shifted from outright denial toward delay, deflection, and exaggerated individual responsibility. It is also right that systemic policy is indispensable, but personal demand changes and technology choices still matter within structural transitions.

claims.claim: Major fossil-fuel interests have funded or used communications that denied, delayed, or deflected climate action despite substantial internal scientific knowledge.
claims.rationale: Internal documents, projections, advertorials, and peer-reviewed communication analyses show a persistent gap between technical knowledge and public framing. The precise conduct and responsibility vary by company and period, so the evidence should not be flattened into one identical conspiracy.

sources.title: Rhetoric and frame analysis of ExxonMobil communications

claims.claim: Modern climate obstruction often emphasizes delay, doom, division, and individual responsibility more than direct denial of basic physics.
claims.rationale: Communication research documents responsibility shifting and delay discourses, while policy debates frequently accept warming but resist specific transitions. The categories overlap, and sincere disagreements about costs or institutions cannot automatically be classified as obstruction.

claims.claim: Systemic policy and collective action are indispensable, while individual behavior alone cannot deliver the required emissions decline.
claims.rationale: Energy, transport, buildings, land use, and industry depend on infrastructure, prices, regulation, and technology systems. Demand-side choices have gigaton-scale potential too, so the best evidence supports interaction rather than a strict individual-versus-system dichotomy.

other_claims: Doom can become an excuse for inaction.
Carbon pricing is one tool rather than a complete climate program.

books.title: Six Degrees
books.subtitle: Our Future on a Hotter Planet
books.author: Mark Lynas
books.summary: The degree-by-degree structure correctly conveys that risks compound sharply with warming and that high-end outcomes become catastrophic. It can imply cleaner thresholds and more deterministic regional sequences than current assessments support.

claims.claim: Climate risks increase nonlinearly with warming, and each additional degree exposes more systems to severe or irreversible harm.
claims.rationale: The IPCC finds rising compound risks, adaptation limits, ecosystem losses, and low-likelihood high-impact outcomes at higher warming levels. Exact risk curves differ by system and region rather than following one universal staircase.

claims.claim: Higher warming increases the chance of crossing thresholds in ice sheets, ecosystems, circulation, and carbon-cycle feedbacks.
claims.rationale: Multiple components exhibit threshold behavior or growing irreversibility, but threshold locations, interaction, timing, and reversibility are often uncertain. A tipping risk is not a calendar prediction of abrupt global collapse.

sources.title: IPCC AR6 global carbon cycles and feedbacks
IPCC ocean and cryosphere special report

claims.claim: A degree-by-degree sequence can reliably predict specific regional social and ecological outcomes.
claims.rationale: Warming levels are useful risk bins and many directional changes are robust. Local precipitation, conflict, migration, crop loss, governance, adaptation, and compound events retain wide ranges, making the structure a scenario guide rather than a deterministic itinerary.

sources.title: IPCC AR6 synthesis summary for policymakers

other_claims: High-emissions futures threaten large-scale displacement.
Avoided warming has value at every level, not only below one threshold.

books.title: The Weather Makers
books.subtitle: How Man Is Changing the Climate and What It Means for Life on Earth
books.author: Tim Flannery
books.summary: Its core attribution, carbon-cycle, and ecological-risk account has aged well. Some particular disaster timing and rapid-threshold rhetoric exceeded what could be supported, while later observations have clarified rather than erased the central warning.

claims.claim: Fossil-fuel burning and land-use change are altering the carbon cycle and driving modern warming.
claims.rationale: Atmospheric measurements, isotopes, ocean uptake, energy-balance evidence, and models firmly attribute the rise in carbon dioxide and most recent warming to human activity.

claims.claim: Warming is already changing water, ice, oceans, species ranges, and extreme-event risk.
claims.rationale: The global directional picture is strong and observed across systems. Event attribution and ecosystem response are probabilistic, and not every drought, storm, fire, or species movement can be assigned primarily to climate change.

claims.claim: Near-term climate feedbacks could produce abrupt, globally transformative outcomes on a relatively precise timetable.
claims.rationale: Feedbacks and abrupt changes are real risk domains, but their onset and magnitude are uncertain and scenario-dependent. Some earlier public predictions about specific imminent outcomes were too confident even though long-run risk has strengthened.

sources.title: IPCC AR6 global carbon cycles and feedbacks
IPCC ocean and cryosphere special report

other_claims: Methane feedbacks can amplify warming.
Australia faces unusually severe heat, fire, and reef risks.

books.title: This Changes Everything
books.subtitle: Capitalism vs. the Climate
books.author: Naomi Klein
books.summary: The book persuasively connects climate delay to fossil-fuel power, deregulation, inequality, and weak public institutions. Its stronger claim that capitalism as such must be displaced is not isolated by comparative evidence, and successful mitigation uses varied mixes of states, markets, movements, and technology.

claims.claim: Market fundamentalism, fossil-fuel political power, and trade or investment constraints have obstructed effective climate policy.
claims.rationale: Production plans, lobbying, infrastructure lock-in, and policy gaps document substantial obstruction and institutional constraint. Effects differ across jurisdictions, and some market instruments and trade rules also accelerate low-carbon deployment.

claims.claim: Climate action can also reduce inequality and improve health, energy access, and democratic capacity when policy is designed for a just transition.
claims.rationale: Mitigation can generate major health and development co-benefits, while badly designed transitions can raise costs or displace workers and communities. Distribution is a policy result, not an automatic property of decarbonization.

claims.claim: Replacing capitalism is necessary for adequate climate mitigation, whereas market-compatible transitions cannot work at required scale.
claims.rationale: The evidence establishes the need for rapid structural change, regulation, public investment, and distributional reform, not one necessary ownership system. Existing low-carbon gains come from mixed institutions, and modeled pathways do not empirically test wholesale system replacement.

other_claims: Extractive sacrifice zones reflect political inequality.
Climate movements can reshape what policies become feasible.

books.title: Drawdown
books.subtitle: The Most Comprehensive Plan Ever Proposed to Reverse Global Warming
books.author: Paul Hawken
books.summary: The portfolio framing is right: electricity, food, land, buildings, transport, industry, and refrigerants all contain scalable mitigation. Ranked gigaton estimates are sensitive to baselines and interactions, and 'reversing' warming requires net-zero carbon dioxide plus durable removal—not a shopping list alone.

claims.claim: Many commercially available measures across energy, food, land, buildings, transport, and industry can deliver large emissions reductions now.
claims.rationale: IPCC and IEA assessments identify substantial near-term potential across all major systems, with several low-cost options. Realized deployment depends on grids, finance, institutions, supply chains, behavior, and local constraints.

sources.title: IPCC AR6 synthesis summary for policymakers

claims.claim: Climate mitigation is a portfolio problem rather than a search for one silver-bullet technology.
claims.rationale: No single sector or technology covers the required reduction. Assessed pathways combine demand, efficiency, clean electricity, electrification, methane cuts, land stewardship, industrial change, and limited carbon removal.

claims.claim: A stable global ranking can state each solution's independent gigaton contribution and cost with high precision.
claims.rationale: Scenario accounting is useful, but solution potentials overlap and depend on baselines, adoption, geography, system boundaries, rebound, learning, and policy. Adding standalone estimates can double count interactions or imply false precision.

sources.title: IPCC agriculture, forestry and land-use mitigation chapter

other_claims: Refrigerant management has unusually high leverage.
Educating girls and reproductive autonomy have broad benefits that should not be reduced to carbon accounting.

books.title: The Wizard and the Prophet
books.subtitle: Two Remarkable Scientists and Their Dueling Visions to Shape Tomorrow's World
books.author: Charles C. Mann
books.summary: The Borlaug–Vogt contrast captures a durable tension between innovation-led abundance and ecological limits. Both mechanisms are real, but the binary understates institutions, inequality, Indigenous knowledge, demand, rebound, and hybrid strategies that dominate actual outcomes.

claims.claim: Agricultural innovation sharply increased yields and helped avert hunger for hundreds of millions.
claims.rationale: Improved varieties, fertilizer, irrigation, agronomy, and policy raised cereal yields and food availability in many regions. Distribution, poverty, conflict, environmental costs, and uneven adoption prevent a simple technology-caused victory over hunger.

sources.title: FAO state of food and agriculture archive

claims.claim: Ecological limits, pollution, soil and water degradation, and biodiversity loss can make growth strategies self-undermining.
claims.rationale: Global assessments document land degradation, freshwater stress, biodiversity loss, nutrient pollution, and climate risks. Limits are heterogeneous and partly movable through technology and governance, not one fixed global carrying-capacity number.

sources.title: FAO land, soil and water resources at stake

claims.claim: Environmental politics is usefully understood as a recurring contest between technological 'wizards' and conservationist 'prophets'.
claims.rationale: The ideal types illuminate real disagreements about substitution, limits, risk, and scale. Most durable policies mix innovation, restraint, rights, prices, public goods, and institutional reform, so the binary is a map rather than an exhaustive causal theory.

other_claims: Borlaug and Vogt shaped competing environmental traditions.
Population outcomes depend on technology, consumption, and distribution together.

books.title: Under a White Sky
books.subtitle: The Nature of the Future
books.author: Elizabeth Kolbert
books.summary: The book accurately shows that attempts to control rivers, species, and climate often create second-order problems requiring further intervention. Its geoengineering cases are real research options, but neither carbon removal nor solar modification substitutes cleanly for rapid emissions cuts.

claims.claim: Large environmental interventions often create unintended ecological effects that prompt additional rounds of management.
claims.rationale: River engineering, invasive-species control, habitat fragmentation, and biocontrol repeatedly produce feedbacks and tradeoffs. This does not make intervention futile; it makes monitoring, reversibility, and adaptive governance central.

claims.claim: Carbon dioxide removal may be needed alongside deep emissions cuts, but current methods face scale, permanence, cost, and ecological constraints.
claims.rationale: Assessed pathways use some removal to balance residual emissions or achieve net-negative carbon dioxide. Potential varies widely, and heavy dependence creates land, energy, storage, governance, and reversal risks.

sources.title: IPCC carbon removal and solar modification

claims.claim: Solar radiation modification could cool global mean temperature while leaving major climatic, ecological, and governance risks unresolved.
claims.rationale: Models show that reflecting sunlight could offset some warming, but regional precipitation, ozone, termination, unequal effects, ocean acidification, legitimacy, and governance remain serious. No evidence supports treating deployment as a tested substitute for mitigation.

sources.title: IPCC international cooperation and solar radiation modification
IPCC impacts technical summary on solar radiation modification

other_claims: Gene editing expands conservation choices while creating new risks.
A managed planet still cannot make every ecological value compatible.
